sources.name: USDA Forest Service EDW Recreation Opportunities GIS — Highway 142 River Access, recarea 21706
observations: Feature objectid 6729 / recarea 21706 identifies Highway 142 River Access on Mark Twain National Forest and publishes coordinates 36.550194,-91.191532, matching all four route occurrences exactly.

Its description calls the site The Narrows and the final take-out for the Eleven Point National Scenic River, 8.7 miles below Riverton; it lists a single-lane concrete ramp, paved parking, and vault toilet.
The feature activity is non-motorized boating and its current Forest Service status field is open.
sources.limits: The GIS feature is a managed recreation-site point and does not state that the coordinate is the exact water-edge toe.

sources.name: Missouri Department of Transportation — Route 142 bridge and access project
observations: MoDOT identifies the east-side Narrows property as the Highway 142 Eleven Point River Access and describes it as a developed site with a single-lane concrete boat ramp and paved parking.
The project page says the river access and bridge will be temporarily closed during part of planned construction; verify the Forest Service and MoDOT status before travel.
sources.limits: MoDOT corroborates the access area and facilities but does not publish an exact access coordinate or wet-toe location.

sources.name: Missouri Department of Conservation — Eleven Point River access directions
observations: MDC lists The Narrows (142) among the lower-river accesses and gives directions from Highway 142.
sources.limits: MDC confirms the named public access and route context, not a precise coordinate.

sources.name: USGS National Hydrography Dataset Large Scale — targeted refreshed route-distance audits
observations: The access point is 271–308 feet from matched Eleven Point River flowlines and within 300 feet of mapped water across the targeted reports.
The selected Cane Bluff-to-Narrows route refresh still reports exceededTransferLimit for its waterbody and route-network queries; the other three route reports have zero source issues.
sources.limits: Incomplete hydrography coverage prevents a full network-proximity conclusion for the Cane Bluff route; access identity is established independently by Forest Service, MoDOT, and MDC sources.

decision: Keep the Forest Service coordinate and add it as an authoritative access-area anchor. The exact wet toe is not separately verified, and the Cane Bluff route's two NHD queries remain truncated.
